content:
TYPE_COL <- "Stype"

#Sidebar dropdown filters
FILTER_DROPDOWNS <- c(cmajor = "cmajor",
                      bfirstgen = "first_gen",
                      Group1 = "Group1",
                      Group2 = "Group2")

filter_choices <- function(df, col, dicts) {
  v <- if (col %in% names(df)) df[[col]] else character(0)
  vals <- unique(v[nzchar(v)])
  vl <- dicts$value_labels
  labs <- vl$label[match(paste(col, vals, sep = "\r"), vl$key)]
  labs[is.na(labs) | !nzchar(labs)] <- vals[is.na(labs) | !nzchar(labs)]
  o <- order(labs)
  c("All" = "All", setNames(vals[o], labs[o]))
}

#Apply sidebar
apply_filters <- function(f, inp) {
  df <- f$kept
  active <- function(x) length(x) == 1 && !is.na(x) && nzchar(trimws(x)) && x != "All"
  col_of <- function(col) if (col %in% names(df)) df[[col]] else rep("", nrow(df))
  has_text <- function(col, x) grepl(tolower(trimws(x)), tolower(col_of(col)), fixed = TRUE)
  
  keep <- rep(TRUE, nrow(df))
  if (active(inp$LN17)) keep <- keep & has_text("LN17", inp$LN17)
  if (active(inp$Advisor)) keep <- keep & has_text("Advisor", inp$Advisor)
  if (active(inp$bstudid)) keep <- keep & trimws(col_of("bstudidC2")) == trimws(inp$bstudid)
  if (active(inp$LN_init)) keep <- keep & toupper(substr(trimws(col_of("LN17")), 1, 1)) == inp$LN_init
  
  for (col in names(FILTER_DROPDOWNS)) {
    v <- inp[[FILTER_DROPDOWNS[[col]]]]
    if (active(v)) keep <- keep & col_of(col) == v
  }
  
  f$n_filtered_out <- sum(!keep)
  f$kept <- df[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  f$n_kept <- sum(keep)
  f
}

TEMPLATES <- list(
  first_year = list(
    label    = "First Year Advising Report",
    file     = "typst/first_year_advising_report.typ",
    values   = c("First-Year"),
    basename = "first_year_reports",
    fields   = c("bstudidC2", "hcalc13", "hapcl13", "cmajcol", "cchoice17")
  ),
  transfer = list(
    label    = "Transfer Advising Report",
    file     = "typst/transfer_advising_report.typ",
    values   = "Transfer/Older",
    basename = "transfer_reports",
    fields   = c("bstudidC2", "ttrnsfr_cr", "cmajcol", "tmilitary", "tyrscmpl")
  )
)

filter_by_type <- function(df, type_key) {
  keep <- df[[TYPE_COL]] %in% TEMPLATES[[type_key]]$values
  list(kept = df[keep, , drop = FALSE], n_total = nrow(df),
       n_kept = sum(keep), n_skipped = sum(!keep))
}

# Transliteration is done with explicit tables rather than
# iconv(x, to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT") because iconv's transliteration is
# supplied by the platform's iconv implementation, and webR (musl/emscripten)
# does not behave like desktop Windows R. Since production runs in webR, the
# mapping has to be ours. Escapes rather than literal characters so this file
# survives being read under any locale.

# Letters that expand to more than one ASCII character. These must run
# before chartr(), which is strictly one-to-one.
.TRANSLIT_MULTI <- c(
  "\u00df" = "ss",  # sharp s
  "\u00e6" = "ae",  # ae ligature
  "\u00c6" = "AE",  # AE ligature
  "\u0153" = "oe",  # oe ligature
  "\u0152" = "OE",  # OE ligature
  "\u00fe" = "th",  # thorn
  "\u00de" = "Th",  # Thorn
  "\u00f0" = "d",  # eth
  "\u00d0" = "D"  # Eth
)

#Letters that map one-to-one
.TRANSLIT_FROM <- paste0(
  "\u00c0\u00c1\u00c2\u00c3\u00c4\u00c5",  # A: grave acute circumflex tilde diaeresis ring
  "\u00c8\u00c9\u00ca\u00cb",  # E
  "\u00cc\u00cd\u00ce\u00cf",  # I
  "\u00d1",  # N tilde
  "\u00d2\u00d3\u00d4\u00d5\u00d6\u00d8",  # O, incl. O with stroke
  "\u00d9\u00da\u00db\u00dc",  # U
  "\u00dd",  # Y acute
  "\u00c7",  # C cedilla
  "\u00e0\u00e1\u00e2\u00e3\u00e4\u00e5",  # a
  "\u00e8\u00e9\u00ea\u00eb",  # e
  "\u00ec\u00ed\u00ee\u00ef",  # i
  "\u00f1",  # n tilde
  "\u00f2\u00f3\u00f4\u00f5\u00f6\u00f8",  # o, incl. o with stroke
  "\u00f9\u00fa\u00fb\u00fc",  # u
  "\u00fd\u00ff",  # y acute / diaeresis
  "\u00e7",  # c cedilla
  "\u0160\u0161\u017d\u017e\u0141\u0142"  # S/s caron, Z/z caron, L/l stroke
)
.TRANSLIT_TO <- paste0(
  "AAAAAA",
  "EEEE",
  "IIII",
  "N",
  "OOOOOO",
  "UUUU",
  "Y",
  "C",
  "aaaaaa",
  "eeee",
  "iiii",
  "n",
  "oooooo",
  "uuuu",
  "yy",
  "c",
  "SsZzLl"
)
stopifnot(nchar(.TRANSLIT_FROM) == nchar(.TRANSLIT_TO))

transliterate <- function(x) {
  for (i in seq_along(.TRANSLIT_MULTI)) {
    x <- gsub(names(.TRANSLIT_MULTI)[i], .TRANSLIT_MULTI[[i]], x, fixed = TRUE)
  }
  chartr(.TRANSLIT_FROM, .TRANSLIT_TO, x)
}

slug <- function(x) {
  x <- transliterate(x)
  x <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "-", x)
  gsub("(^-|-$)", "", x)
}

# mode is "name" (FN17-LN17.pdf) or "id" (bstudidC2.pdf). Names can collide,
# so de-duplicate; IDs are unique by construction but the same pass is
# harmless.
make_filenames <- function(df, mode = "name") {
  base <- if (identical(mode, "id")) {
    slug(df$bstudidC2)
  } else {
    slug(paste(df$FN17, df$LN17))
  }

  # A name with nothing transliterable in it (e.g. entirely non-Latin script)
  # slugs to "". That is not merely an ugly filename: assign("", ...) in the
  # de-duplication loop below raises "attempt to use zero-length variable
  # name", which aborts the WHOLE batch rather than one row. Fall back to the
  # student ID, which is unique by construction.
  empty <- !nzchar(base)
  if (any(empty)) {
    fallback <- slug(df$bstudidC2[empty])
    fallback[!nzchar(fallback)] <- "report"
    base[empty] <- fallback
  }

  seen <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  vapply(base, function(b) {
    n <- (if (is.null(seen[[b]])) 0 else seen[[b]]) + 1
    assign(b, n, envir = seen)
    if (n == 1) paste0(b, ".pdf") else sprintf("%s-%d.pdf", b, n)
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}


# Builds the payload sent to JS via session$sendCustomMessage("compile_typst", ...).
# root lets callers (tests) point the file reads somewhere other than the
# project root without changing app.R's own behaviour (root defaults to ".",
# matching app.R's cwd-relative reads).
build_compile_message <- function(kept, tpl, dicts, filename_mode = "name", root = ".") {
  rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(kept)), function(i) {
    decode_row(as.list(kept[i, , drop = FALSE]), dicts)
  })

  list(
    sharedTemplate = paste(readLines(file.path(root, "typst/BCSSE_template.typ"), warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n"),
    mainTemplate = paste(readLines(file.path(root, tpl$file), warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n"),
    rows = as.character(jsonlite::toJSON(rows, auto_unbox = TRUE)),
    filenames = I(make_filenames(kept, filename_mode)),
    zipName = paste0(tpl$basename, ".zip")
  )
}

tally_message <- function(f, type_key) {
  label <- TEMPLATES[[type_key]]$label
  n_filt <- if (is.null(f$n_filtered_out)) 0 else f$n_filtered_out
  if (f$n_kept == 0 && n_filt > 0) {
    return(sprintf("No %s rows match the current filters (%d removed by filters).",
                   label, n_filt))
  }
  if (f$n_kept == 0) {
    other <- setdiff(names(TEMPLATES), type_key)[1]
    return(sprintf(
      "No rows match %s. This file has %d row(s) of another type - did you mean %s?",
      label, f$n_total, TEMPLATES[[other]]$label
    ))
  }
  msg <- sprintf("%d rows; %d match %s, %d skipped.",
                 f$n_total, f$n_kept, label, f$n_skipped)
  if (n_filt > 0) msg <- paste(msg, sprintf("%d more excluded by filters.", n_filt))
  msg
}

content:
#import "BCSSE_template.typ": *

#show: report.with(title: "First-Year Student Advising Report")

#let row = json("/data.json")
#let row = row + (full_name: field(row, "FN17") + " " + field(row, "LN17"))

The Beginning College Survey of Student Engagement Student Advising Report is
an individualized report for students and is designed to help advisors
understand how student expectations about college activities and learning
might affect their academic experiences. Information about using the BCSSE
Advising report can be found at: bcsse.indiana.edu.

#grid(
  columns: (1fr, 1fr),
  rows: auto,
  inset: (x, y) => if x == 0 { (right: 9pt) } else { (left: 9pt) },
  grid.vline(x: 1, stroke: 0.5pt + muted.lighten(40%)),
  grid.cell[
#section(
  "Student Background",
  row: row,
  items: (
    ("full_name", "Name"),
    ("bstudidC2", "Student ID"),
    ("hcalc13", "Completed Calculus"),
    ("hapcl13", "Advanced Placement (AP)"),
    ("cmajor", "Expected Major"),
    ("cchoice17", "Institution Choice"),
  ),
)
// This item needs to be three columns - one for HS and one for FY expected
#section(
  "Hours per Week (during high school and expected)",
  headers: ("High school", "Expected"),
  row: row,
  items: (
    ("hacadpr13", "cacadpr13", "Studying"),
    ("hwork", "cwork", "Working"),
    ("hcocurr", "ccocurr", "Co-curricular"),
    ("hsocial13", "csocial13", "Socializing/relaxing"),
  ),
)

#section(
  "High School Challenge",
  row: row,
  items: (
    ("hchallenge", "To what extent did your courses challenge you to do your best work?"),
  ),
)

#section(
  "First-Year Expectations",
  row: row + (EXP_SFI: fmt-scale(row.at("EXP_SFI", default: ""))) + 
  (EXP_DD: fmt-scale(row.at("EXP_DD", default: ""))) + 
  (EXP_CL: fmt-scale(row.at("EXP_CL", default: ""))),
  items: (
    ("EXP_SFI", "Student-Faculty Interaction"),
    ("EXP_DD", "Interaction with Diverse Others"),
    ("EXP_CL", "Peer Collaboration"),
  ),
)

#section(
  "Expected Academic Help-Seeking",
  prompt: "How often expect to seek help with coursework from:",
  scale: "1 = Never; 2 = Sometimes; 3 = Often; 4 = Very Often",
  row:row,
  items: (
    ("cseekfac", "Faculty members"),
    ("cseekaa", "Academic advisors"), 
    ("cseekls", "Learning Support Services (tutoring, writing center, success coaching, etc.)"),
    ("cseekfrnd", "Friends or other students"),
    ("cseekfam", "Family members"),
    ("cseekoth", "Other persons or offices"),
  ),
)
],
grid.cell[
#section(
  "Expected Transition Difficulty",
  prompt: "How difficult do you expect the following to be:",
  scale: "1 = Not at all difficult to 6 = Very difficult",
  row:row,
  items: (
    ("clearnma", "Learning course material"),

an individualized report for students and is designed to help advisors
understand how student expectations about college activities and learning
might affect their academic experiences. Information about using the BCSSE
Advising report can be found at: bcsse.indiana.edu.
